In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a serum-free, chemically-defined system for hepatocarcinaogenesis, which is a model of HBV infection in vivo.

the study of hepatocarcinogenetic mechanisms in vitro, using a cell line which may be considered a model for in vivo hepatocarcinoma, in order to obtain information on the role of HBV infection in the development of human hepatocellular carcinoma.
the study of the effect of hormones and growth factors on PLC/PRF/F human hepatoma cells, in order to obtain a model for the study of hepatocarcinogenes and HBV gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PLC/PRF5 cell line is an excellent tool for the study both on the mechanism of HBV replication and on the role of HBV in hepatocarcinogenisis, as well as for the study of the effect of drugs on HBV infection.

the serum-free growth of PLC/PRFs human hepatoma cells is a useful system in which the effects of hormones, growth factors, or other substances on cell growth, HBsAg production and HBV DNA synthesis can be studied.
PLC/PRF5 cells are a good model system for studies on hepatocarcinogenic mechanisms and HBV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PLC/PRF5 cells grown in a defined, serum-free medium are a good model system for the study of the role of growth factors and hormones in hepatocarcinoma, and for the evaluation of the effect of drugs on hepatocarcinomas.

PLC/PRF5 human hepatoma cell growth is stimulated by insulin, epidermal growth factor and dexamethasone, whereas the HBsAg production is enhanced by insulin and epidermal growth factors and is reduced by dexamethasome.
PLC/PRF5 cells can be used as a model for the study of hepatocellular carcinoma and of the role of hepatitis B virus in its development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PLC/PRF5 cells can be grown in a serum- and hormone-free medium and this may be used as an in vitro model for studying hepatocarcinogenetic processes and virus gene expression.
the PLC/PRF5 cell line may be a useful tool in the study of hepatocarcinogenic mechanisms and in the search of new therapeutic approaches.
the PLC/PRF human hepatoma cells can be grown in serum free medium, which allows for the study of hepatocarcinogenisis and HBV infection.
